reviews.text:
Elizabeth and her team are phenomenal. We found her when we were having the dreaded puppy blues with our baby Aussie girl, Piggy. She was so gentle with us with us as we wear nearing burn out.

Elizabeth has a solid philosophy that works. She teaches at a pace that is perfect for new and previous dog owners alike. So far we have done puppy training, learned crate & potty training, lots of socialization, simple leash directions, sit, lay down, spin, roll over, follow me, this way, et al.

Piggy learned so fast; she's just nine months old but so far she's mastered the baseline of having a happy, healthy, well adjusted dog.

The biggest takeaway for me a second time dog owner was the important of building confidence in a young dog, positive reinforcement, socialization, chewing & licking to settle themselves, et al.

We will be back from teen puppy and adult training in the fall and we're so pumped to build on what we know.

I couldn't have been luckier to bump into Elizabeth. She found me struggling to walk Moses (a new pit doggo i'm fostering) and immediately took us in, gave him a harness (he chewed through his last one from his last foster home) and treats. Then, she taught me how to hold him, walk him, and the first steps of training him. Before I met Elizabeth, Moses was dragging me around and I had lower back pain just from the 16 hours I've had him for. Now, (1 day later) I felt comfortable walking him from south williamsburg to Radio Bakery in Greenpoint. I would recommend everyone, especially new dog owners, to go to The Dog Institute. I was so overwhelmed by Moses and now I can comfortable take him out and know that I'm teaching him the right habits, making it easier for him to find his forever home.

What can I say, I wish I could enroll in The Dog Institute, and would probably be better at parties for it.

In all seriousness, after my dog passed four years ago I thought I would never adopt a pup again, partly from heartbreak but also because I have a bossy take no prisoners cat named Mom Cat who has limited mobility and a long sharp set of active claws. But then I met Bruce. Bruce is a rescue pit puppy from a litter rescued from a backyard breeder in NJ that I happened to meet at Honeys in Brooklyn. The rescue called The Good Dog Rescue let me take him for two weeks to see if he could charm Mom Cat, hopeful because he had been fostered with 14 dogs and... "some ferrets." Well, Bruce luckily was a perfect gentleman with mom cat but sitting in my apartment I looked over at him while he gnawed on a dandelion green and realized Bruce deserved more than what me, a semi depressive tenants rights attorney, and a decidedly un-maternal grumpy cat could offer.

Bruce needed friends, a community, and the opportunity to play, learn, and be showered with love, affection, structure, and freeze dried chicken breast strips as often and enthusiastically as and as possible. The next day I brought Bruce to Elizabeth at The Dog Institute. She immediately helped me identify strategies to make sure he and mom cat could develop their relationship while feeling safe and secure, helped me with walking, tethering, and crate training, as well as dialing in a food and treat program to keep him happy and active as well as avoiding foods that might be causing skin irritation. The three modes of training she developed and the care with which she teaches you them is so positive, thorough, comprehensive, confidence building for Bruce (and myself.) The classes on Sundays are creative and exploratory and responsive to the vibe of the group. But Bruce's favorite is the Play and Train sessions Monday through Thursday. He literally smiles when we pull up at 9 am SO excited to play with his friends, learn about impulse control, pose for handsome portraits, and listen to whatever calming avant guard music is on the speakers that day.

Bruce is in LOVE with everyone who works there and turns into a wiggling ball of joy if he sees Elizabeth, Allie, Masami, Roshni, Maria, or Lacy on the corner. (So do I.) I get daily reports and videos and class pics every day. It has been such an honor and relief to have such a supportive, caring, and joyful community looking out for Bruce as he grows up. If you have any pup questions, are facing any challenges, or just want to make your pup skip around with happiness do not wait, GO straight to The Dog Institute.

Could not have had a better experience. The Dog Institute took the stress out of being a first time dog owner so that I could focus on the joy of raising a puppy. I did individual training and puppy school. The training was hands-on and accommodative. Elizabeth is wonderful and VERY knowledgeable. My frenchie loved going to school and there is a strong sense of community for the pawrents I really enjoyed. An absolute gem in the neighborhood.

Started bringing our (now) 13 wk old pup here a few weeks ago for puppy socialization classes and it's already so clear that it was the best "new parent" decision we could've made. We signed up for the Puppy Curriculum which comes with 1:1 training, and Elizabeth is thorough, patient, kind and so generous with her guidance and time helping us learn to read the cues, adjust our approach where needed, and confidently learn to train our new girl. You can tell everyone on her team really cares and is invested in all the puppies who attend classes. It's an awesome community. And best of all, our pup is obsessed. Highly recommend!

The best thing you can do for your dog. Elizabeth and her team go above and beyond. They are genuinely loving and caring, and they've built an environment where puppies can learn how to play and socialize with others. Watch how excited your dog gets when you arrive, and you'll know you'll be coming back.

Elizabeth and her team at The Dog Institute of Williamsburg are the best. Their warmth, communication and expertise makes every interaction feel both thoughtful and personal. After only a few training sessions and play and train classes, we noticed such a positive difference in our puppy!!

We cannot recommend The Dog Institute enough!!! Elizabeth is so knowledgable and the facetime sessions were incredibly helpful for us learning how to train our puppy at home in between sessions with her. The play and train classes have been amazing too, teaching our puppy how to play with other dogs and the entire staff has been so amazing. He gets so excited whenever we get close to The Dog Institute! Elizabeth has been so great to work with, always there to answer any questions and she always has a solution that works beautifully. We can't wait to keep working with her as our puppy continues to grow!

The Dog Institute is truly exceptional. From the moment I first spoke with Elizabeth, the owner, I knew we had found the right place to support us after bringing home our American Shepherd puppy, Ruby. In that very first phone conversation, Elizabeth could hear the uneasiness in my voice. I was feeling overwhelmed and stressed about doing everything right to raise our puppy well and give her a great life. Elizabeth immediately put me at ease with her calm, thoughtful approach and clear depth of experience.

Since then, The Dog Institute has been an incredible resource for us. Ruby attends Play & Train regularly, and it’s easily her favorite thing in the world. The staff are fantastic: friendly, attentive, and clearly very experienced with a wide range of dogs and personalities. It’s such a positive, well-run environment, and we always feel confident knowing Ruby is spending time with such a great group of people and dogs.

We also work with Elizabeth for Ruby’s 1:1 training sessions. Her knowledge and experience really shine in how clearly and effectively she teaches both dogs and their owners. The sessions are practical, approachable, and incredibly effective. Ruby soaked up her early lessons and quickly grew into a confident, well-behaved puppy thanks to Elizabeth’s guidance.

We feel so lucky to have found The Dog Institute and are incredibly grateful for Elizabeth and the entire team. We’re excited to continue working with them as Ruby grows.

Elizabeth is an incredible trainer! I call her the puppy whisperer because she gets puppy’s trained so quickly. And she cares so much about each pups wellbeing - her puppy socialization classes are unmatched. I would trust her with my pups training and life. Her team is also incredible and take care and love the pups. I couldn’t recommend her more. She has also helped us as new first time dog owners learn to train our dog and build a philosophy and approach to taking care of them.

If you’re planning to get a new puppy, don’t hesitate to enroll in training with Elizabeth and her team at the Dog Institute. I grew up with dogs and did plenty of prep before bringing home my sheltie, Oslo but there is truly no way I would have been set up for success without Elizabeth. The intro lessons went far beyond basic commands. They helped me thoughtfully set up my home, routine, and expectations for life with a new puppy in Brooklyn.

Along the way, we made practical adjustments to everything - my daily schedule, feeding routine, crate size, harness and gear all tailored specifically to Oslo. I got endless insight into the types of enrichment toys that would suit Oslo to which pet stores in the neighborhood have the best chews. Elizabeth has a wealth of knowledge and an incredibly thoughtful approach. She doesn’t just teach skills, she empowers you with the confidence and toolkit you need to raise a well-adjusted, happy pup in NYC. Despite lifelong dog experience, that guidance was invaluable for me.

Oslo loves nothing more than his Play & Train sessions. He literally runs into class and sometimes even tries to lead me to the Dog Institute on our walks. The structure of supervised play with both puppies and well-mannered adult dogs has done wonders for his confidence and social skills.

I also feel completely at ease leaving Oslo with Elizabeth and her team. Many of the dogs are regulars, which creates a safe, familiar environment that gives me so much peace of mind. Not to mention plenty of adorable photo and video updates.

Elizabeth was so accommodating with me and my dog. I have a senior dog who is a little cray cray and Elizabeth was so understanding. She helped me even before our first session with so many tips and tricks of how to handle her. She was patient, clear with her instructions, and made sure that she was accessible for me to reach out to when needed. Thank you Elizabeth!!🐾

Elizabeth and everyone at the Dog Institute of Williamsburg were wonderful. We went to them for help training our four-month-old puppy Milo, and they were incredibly helpful from start to finish. The training was very in-depth and detailed, and it made a huge difference for us.

It was especially great to see how confident our son became through the process—he felt empowered to help train our puppy and really took pride in it. We couldn’t be happier with the experience and highly recommend them.

We originally planned to foster our little pittie mix and wanted to set him up for success with his future family. He’d already been through so much by 3 months old with an injured paw, very scared, reactive, but always loving.

The Dog Institute truly brought him out of his shell. Teacher Ally and Roshni will be his aunties for life, and Elizabeth helped us build an incredible relationship with him. She taught us how to meet him with acceptance and use positive reinforcement to help him work through his fears. To be honest she helped us work through our own fears and weird programming at the same time.

It was the best investment we ever made, because he ended up staying with us. We can’t imagine life without him. Thank you, TDI! 💛

There are places that care for dogs… and then there is Dog Institute — a place that loves them with heart and soul. Elizabeth is pure magic. She doesn’t just train dogs — she understands them, feels them, and connects with them on the deepest level. It’s rare and beautiful to witness.
Our sweet Monia has blossomed so much thanks to her. The care is five-star, the environment is loving, and the mental stimulation is incredible. We are endlessly grateful. If you’re a dog lover, this place will change your life.
Forever thankful,
Renata and Boris

I can’t praise Elizabeth and her team more! I got a cavapoo puppy in October and don’t know what I would do without the Dog Institute, they have been so incredible, especially as a first time mom. Elizabeth is amazing and was so thorough and dedicated in our puppy training sessions. Hazel has been going to the play & train sessions and it is by far the highlight of her week. They take the best care of all the puppies there and I feel so comfortable leaving here as I know she is in good hands. She is the happiest there playing with all her friends. Highly recommend!

Elizabeth and team are the absolute best! The puppy classes have been the best investment I could have made to have Chevy (bottom left with blue collar) socialized early and often. The virtual training sessions & board/train programs have also been instrumental in turning Chevy into a standup gentlemen even as a 7 month old rescue.

If you’re considering the Dog Institute, I can share from my experience that this is THE place to send your puppy. Elizabeth is a trusted resource and she makes everything extremely personable and accommodating. Not only has she been an amazing trainer, but she’s also been extremely helpful when it comes to his health (almost as much if not more as my vet!).

Can go on and on about how amazing my experience has been - bottom line is I’d highly highly recommend especially for first time owners!
When we got Clio and need direction, this place was our savior. She taught Clio to behave and how to be a well trained pup of society. Thank you so much for all of your help.

Incredible place, especially for puppy training. We felt so well taken care of and the techniques we learned really helped our dog adapt to life in Brooklyn. She is a cavapoo and 5 years later we still come back to so many of the tools that Elizabeth taught us especially since we had a baby a couple of years ago. She has been really generous with additional guidance and was flexible with our sessions. Cannot recommend more highly. The sitting facilities and dog supplies they have are also super high quality — our lead from there is still in great shape after 4 years of daily use!!!!

I’ve had such a great experience working with Elizabeth! She’s been amazing at helping me understand my dog Zeppelin’s behavior and giving me the right tools to support him. I’ve learned so much throughout our sessions, and I can really see how much Zeppelin has grown — he’s calmer, more confident, and responds so much better now. Elizabeth is patient, knowledgeable, and genuinely cares about helping both dogs and owners succeed. I’m so grateful for everything she’s taught us!

We’ve been going to Dog Institute regularly for almost two years with our miniature poodle pup (Coco) for play and train as well as boarding and cannot recommend it enough!!

Our normally socially nervous pup LOVES going there and has really bonded with the whole team (both of the Elizabeth’s, Allie, Masami, Maria).  Everyone who works there is extremely kind and gentle with all the dogs and you can tell they truly love working with them.  You can tell when you drop your pup off by how much they want to be there as well as the many photo and video updates you get (it never gets old when they put the party hats on all the dogs when it’s one of their birthdays 🥰)

We also really appreciated too that when Coco was a baby and we’d have issues, Elizabeth would ask a lot of questions to understand the situation before giving advice (for example around crate training, having issues with accidents only when at guest houses, becoming territorial of us) - the result is we have a very happy and sweet pup who is well socialized.

They’ve been really amazing and you won’t regret taking your pup there!!

Dog Institute has been such a positive experience for our Barbet puppy Boots. Amazing way to socialize a puppy in a controlled and safe environment, with good natured playmates and professional supervision. Our pup absolutely loves his days at school, the friendly staff, and his puppy friends.

We’ve gotten so much out of our sessions with Elizabeth, for first time dog owners we found a lot of benefit in the structure she provided for Boots’ home life (crate, food, schedule, etc.). We’ve seen such positive results from the Puppy curriculum that we’ve enrolled Boots in the adolescent training as well. Highly recommend!
